properties.name: The 9 remaining unattributed defect acknowledgements were backfilled to who:ajs
properties.rationale:
⚠️ NO `acted_at`, FOR THE SAME REASON AS THE 117 — see `chg:117-historical-gap-acknowledgements-attributed-to-ajs`, which carries the argument in full. In short: the real judgement dates run back to 2026-07-24 and were never recorded per-acknowledgement, so null is the only true value; and #368's root cause turned on the DATE DISTRIBUTION of existing approver edges, which synthetic same-day stamps would destroy.

THE ONE THING WORTH ADDING HERE, because the defect side is where #368's evidence actually sat: its three attributed defect acknowledgements are dated 2026-08-29, the day `acknowledge_defect_by` shipped. That is now the whole dated population on this side, and the 9 added here are deliberately not in it. Anyone re-running that analysis reads 3 dated and 9 undated, which is the truth: the parameter was used the day it existed, and everything older predates it.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT THAT SURVIVES BOTH BACKFILLS: the zeroes #368 measured were never negligence. On the defect side there was no field to fill until this morning; on the gap side there was none until 2026-08-23. Attribution followed the parameter in both families, which is what made the ABSENT PARAMETER the cause rather than the caller. Backfilling the history does not weaken that finding — it completes the record the parameter could not have carried.
properties.subject: record
properties.summary:
The 9 `decision:ack:heal:*` acknowledgements that still carried no approver were given AUTHORED_BY role=approver to who:ajs, on Anthony's word this session. With #368's three, the defect family is now 12/12 attributed — closing the residue that PR measured as "acknowledge_defect NO param, 12 acknowledgements, 0 attributed". Together with the 117 gap acknowledgements done earlier today, every acknowledgement in this design now says whose judgement it was.

THE SET WAS READ BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN. Six say so explicitly in their own text — "Carries dec:graph-spof-accepted (2026-07-24)", and the same for core-api, the export door, ifc:graph-export, cmp:service and cmp:sanitize — so those are Anthony's accepted Decisions being carried onto the reviewed-defects mechanism. A seventh (`decision:ack:heal:d6d4f53469211481`) rests on `dec:one-surface` the same way. TWO ARE AGENT READINGS OF DECISIONS HE HAD ALREADY ACCEPTED RATHER THAN DIRECT STATEMENTS, and that is recorded rather than smoothed over: `decision:ack:heal:4b023a9e7da76757` declines to manufacture a follow-through between two `proposed` requirements, applying `dec:certainty-derived`; and `decision:ack:heal:4bd7c50f777fe56e` is marked "ACKNOWLEDGED UNDER PROTEST" — the protest being that the contradiction IS resolved by `dec:the-stranded-server-correction-stands` and the detector cannot see it. Both dispositions follow from accepted Decisions of his, which is why they are attributed to him; neither is a judgement he stated in those words.
